scope.note: Phase 3 scope. The real Stage 4 stores 512 programs in 8 banks and has a separate per-section preset library; this benchmark deliberately cuts that to one bank of 32 programs and no preset library. Items under excluded are never required; their panel controls exist visually but stay decorative and are listed as unsupported.
required: 32 program slots: 4 pages of 8, selected with the Program buttons and Page buttons
Program dial browsing and a numeric list view
Store and Store As (with naming), dirty-state indicator, edit-discard on program change
Splits with up to 4 zones, 3 editable split points, and crossfades
Wheel and Control Pedal morph assignment
Master Clock (tap and dial), Transpose, Panic
optional: Alphabetic list sorting, program categories, Solo, and multi-view Prog View modes
Single-level undo for program change from an edited state
excluded: Banks beyond one, the 512-program factory bank layout, and Organize swap/move (manual p. 41, 45)
Aftertouch as a morph source (browser keyboards have no aftertouch; the A.T. button stays decorative)
Num Pad mode, Monitor/Copy/Paste/Swap, Section Edit, Layer Init (manual p. 43-44)
Aux KB, Extern, memory protection, and every Shift-menu (System/Sound/Organize/Output/Pedal/MIDI) (manual p. 44, 57-63)
External MIDI clock sync and pedal tap (manual p. 40)

includes: Piano, Organ, and Synth sound selection and parameters
Effect settings, targeting, and rotary routing
programState.dirtyState: An edited program shows an E indicator; selecting another program without storing discards the edits (manual p. 13).

storage.layout: 4 pages of 8 program buttons; the display shows page.button and the name (for example 3.2 Tine Stack).
storage.factoryContent: Ship at least 8 stored factory programs demonstrating piano, organ, synth, split, and layered setups.
storage.store: STORE once flashes and shows the destination; select with dial/page/program buttons (destination becomes audible for auditioning); STORE again confirms; Shift/Exit cancels (manual p. 13).
storage.storeAs: STORE AS opens naming (character entry, insert, delete) before the destination step (manual p. 41).
storage.liveMode: LIVE MODE switches the 8 program buttons to Live slots; all edits are stored automatically; programs can be copied between Live and regular slots via Store (manual p. 13, 44).
storage.listView: Shift plus the Program dial opens a numeric list of all 32 programs (manual p. 41).

split.behavior: SPLIT ON/SET toggles a single Mid split at C4; press-and-hold opens editing for each point's note and crossfade. Split-point LEDs above the keybed show active positions (manual p. 39).
split.zoneAssignment: KB ZONE controls assign any Organ, Piano, or Synth layer to any contiguous zone range; zone LEDs show the assignment (manual p. 39).
split.crossfadeBehavior: Off switches immediately at the split point; ±6/±12 fade sounds across that many semitones on each side (manual p. 39).

layerScenes.behavior: Two independent layer on/off configurations within one program; sound parameters are shared, only enable state differs. The LAYER SCENE II LED shows the active scene (manual p. 43).

morph.controlPedalInput: A virtual on-screen pedal and MIDI CC11 both drive the Control Pedal source.
morph.assignment: Hold (or double-tap to latch) a morph source button, then move destination controls from start to end value; multiple destinations per source; a morph may increase one destination while decreasing another (manual p. 38-39).
morph.clear: Shift plus the source button clears all of that source's assignments; re-holding and zeroing a control removes a single assignment (manual p. 39).
morph.indicators: Assigned knobs light their green morph LED; level faders and drawbars show the morphed range on their LED graphs (manual p. 39).

set: tap the MST CLK button four or more times
hold it and dial a BPM

clockAndPerformance.panic: Shift+Transpose sends an internal All Notes Off and resets held performance inputs (manual p. 40).

acceptance: Storing and re-loading any of the 32 programs round-trips all supported piano, organ, synth, effect, routing, split, scene, and morph state, and the dirty indicator is truthful.
Moving a morph source interpolates every assigned destination and updates its hardware indicator; clearing works per source.
Split positions, zone assignments, and crossfades are editable from the panel and audibly route notes, not fixed constants.
Layer Scene I/II toggles enable state without duplicating or losing sound parameters.
Live slots persist edits automatically and survive reload; Master Clock, Transpose, and Panic behave as specified.
